answer_1.quote: Generating descriptions from semantic graphs is an important application of Natural Language Generation (NLG) and can be framed in a graph-to-text transduction approach.
answer_1.outputs: Three sentences are generated per input graph, forming a set of descriptions.

answer_2.quote: The quality evaluation scores (BLEU:, CHRF++:) are calculated based on the average score of the three outputs. The diversity evaluation scores (Self-BLEU, Multi-Score) are computed using the three outputs.

answer_4.quote: To further assess the quality of the generated sentences from each model, we perform a manual error analysis in a subset of the English test data. We observed three common mistakes from the outputs: Syntax/Spelling Mistake, Lack of Information, Information Redundancy.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked to examine each generated sentence and identify whether it contained a Syntax/Spelling mistake, lacked information from the input graph, or exhibited information redundancy.
